root_cause: Discovery skill gives rich how-to-ask guidance and explicit approval-stage silence handling, but no guidance for when a structured interview question is skipped/unanswered, leaving the agent to improvise a less structured fallback.

attribution.rationale: interviewing.md covers how to shape a question and dependency order; SKILL.md covers silence only at the approval stage; the interview-stage skip has no contract, so the agent improvised a long unstructured turn twice.
attribution.possible_misattribution: model-limit: a stronger agent might have treated the recommendation as a provisional assumption and continued without skill guidance.

operations.summary: Add a short subsection on handling an unanswered interview decision: treat the strongest recommendation as a provisional assumption with a named risk, state it, continue dependent work, confirm at final contract approval; do not loop or silently promote.

root_cause: scd-quickdev selects its delivery path once at intake and never re-checks; nothing tells the agent to stop widening the current branch when in-flight debugging crosses the Discovery/Project boundary, so a single bug fix silently grows into an unapproved redesign.

attribution.rationale: The skill has a one-time path-selection gate and only reactive, fragmented scope-drift hints that assume the agent already noticed the drift. In the observed session the agent kept widening one Issue's branch across a different root cause, layer, and finally a user-supplied architecture proposal, instead of recognizing a new Discovery/Project path had emerged.
attribution.possible_misattribution: Agent-limit or requirements: the diagnosing agent could have noticed the drift on its own, and the user's framing stayed terse. Both contributed, but the skill is the only editable lever and the missing rule (re-select path when in-flight scope crosses the Discovery/Project threshold) is the cheapest durable fix.

matched_signals: skill instructions led to scope expansion (bug fix branch widened into adapter, config, and E2E harness work outside the Issue acceptance)
user corrected skill-driven behavior (user pasted own architecture proposal and manually invoked scd-discovery and scd-project to redirect the flow)
unmatched_signals: no deterministic skill script or format failed; the skill prose executed as written
documented trigger matched and skill was invoked correctly for the initial bug delivery
no isolated replay was performed; evidence is a single observation

evidence.summary: A long multi-task session opened as a scd-quickdev bug diagnosis and was delivered cleanly, but the request then evolved into a multi-decision product architecture redesign. The agent kept extending the original Issue's branch with adjacent problems and did not route to scd-discovery until the user manually supplied an architecture proposal and explicitly invoked that skill.

root_cause: scd-uiux delegates all design quality to the eight-dimension checklist, which is a verification frame rather than generation knowledge: no pre-generation direction block, no anti-pattern bans, no concrete numeric thresholds and no token discipline, so visual output regresses to the mean.

attribution.rationale: The user judged scd-uiux design output quality as low. Source analysis of five high-star peer skills (pre-generation decide block plus banned defaults, searchable design knowledge, DTCG three-tier tokens, two-fidelity design loop, dual-persona review) shows this capability class is entirely absent from scd-uiux, whose only design-quality artifact is the shared eight-dimension checklist.
attribution.possible_misattribution: model-limit: a stronger model could compensate with its own taste; but the skill must carry portable design judgment, and the peer-standard gap is structural.

matched_signals: user directly judged scd-uiux output design quality as low and requested comparison with popular high-star skills

unmatched_signals: no interactive failure trace was diagnosed; this is a user-initiated research-backed improvement

evidence.summary: User reported low design quality and asked for popular alternatives; agent read core source files of five high-star repos (design-taste rules with banned defaults, DTCG token architecture, WDS two-fidelity design loop, HIG dual-persona review, context-fidelity discipline) and mapped the shared capability gap onto scd-uiux; user then approved the bounded five-operation checklist and confirmed the candidate ID.

operations.summary: New shared reference: mandatory pre-generation direction block (domain, mood, motion depth, layout family, reference anchor) before any visual artifact; banned-defaults table with reason and replacement per item; mobile-first baseline rule.

New shared reference: three-tier token discipline (primitive, semantic, component; primitives never referenced directly), naming convention, dark mode swapped at the semantic layer, semantic-structure vs visual-style separation.
Hook design-taste.md into the visual-delivery section: direction block required before generating visual artifacts; governance flow unchanged.
Hook design-tokens.md into the visual and component discipline section: token discipline applies when contracts describe visual increments.

Eight-dimension table upgraded to thresholds plus anti-patterns (contrast 4.5:1, touch 44px, headline 2.5x body, measure 45-75ch, 4px spacing ladder, outer greater than inner, one primary one accent); self-review rounds gain direction-decision and change-reason fields.

Two-fidelity loop added to the fidelity table: low fidelity resolves structure and hierarchy only (no typography or color debate), confirmation freezes the reference before high fidelity; discuss before wireframing.
Add a design decision log column to the visual direction and system increment section of the UX contract template.
